intent: I'm tired of gadgets that die in three years. I want to buy one camera now, in my mid-thirties, and still be shooting with it when my kids graduate. I keep hearing shutters have a rated life, weather sealing degrades, and some lens mounts wobble loose, but I don't really know which parts of a camera actually wear out first or why. Long-time owners surely know which models are still going strong after a decade and which turned into paperweights. Money is less of an issue than regret. Walk me through what fails, what lasts, and finish with the body and lens you'd trust for the long haul.
